content: Monitoring for adverse reactions is essential when co-administering drugs that interact with hepatic or renal clearance pathways. 1. Darunavir and Doravirine: Darunavir increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for increased plasma concentrations and potential toxicities. 2. Doravirine and CYP3A4 Inhibitors: Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate doravirine plasma levels, increasing the risk of toxicities. Monitor closely. 3. Dichlorphenamide and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs reduce serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor potassium levels to prevent hypokalemia. 4. Tenofovir DF and Diclofenac: These drugs can increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to toxicity. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 5. Tenofovir DF and NSAIDs: Co-administration with high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen) may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity due to competition for renal excretion. Consider alternatives to NSAIDs and monitor renal function. 6. Tenofovir DF and Didanosine: Tenofovir increases didanosine toxicity by reducing its elimination, potentially causing pancreatitis. Reduce the didanosine dose to 250 mg/day for patients >60 kg and 200 mg/day for those <60 kg. Monitor closely. 7. Tenofovir DF and Digoxin: Tenofovir increases digoxin levels by reducing renal clearance, raising the risk of toxicity. Use caution and monitor digoxin levels. 8. Tenofovir DF and Dofetilide: Tenofovir increases dofetilide levels by reducing renal clearance, which may lead to toxicity. Monitor closely. 9. Tenofovir DF and Duvelisib: Tenofovir decreases duvelisib levels via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 10. Efavirenz and Lamivudine or Tenofovir DF: Both combinations increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor for symptoms. 11. Elagolix and Tenofovir DF or Doravirine: Elagolix increases tenofovir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition and decreases doravirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 12. Enfuvirtide and Lamivudine or Tenofovir DF: Both combinations increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 13. Fedratinib and Doravirine: Fedratinib increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased plasma concentrations and adjust doses as needed. 14. Emtricitabine and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 15. Encorafenib and Tenofovir DF: Encorafenib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase tenofovir levels and associated toxicities. 16. Tenofovir DF and Entecavir: Tenofovir increases entecavir levels by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to toxicity. Monitor closely. 17. Lamivudine and Erdafitinib: Lamivudine increases erdafitinib levels by reducing renal clearance. Consider alternatives or reduce the dose of erdafitinib based on tolerability. 18. Tenofovir DF and NSAIDs (e.g., Etodolac, Flurbiprofen): Co-administration may increase toxicity due to reduced renal clearance. Monitor closely and consider alternatives. 19. Fenofibrate and Tenofovir DF: Fenofibrate increases tenofovir levels by reducing renal clearance, raising the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 20. Flucytosine and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity risks. Monitor renal function and adjust therapy as needed. 21. Fosamprenavir and Lamivudine or Tenofovir DF: Both combinations increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 22. Foscarnet and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity risks. Monitor renal function closely. 23. Ganciclovir and Lamivudine or Tenofovir DF: Ganciclovir increases tenofovir levels and hematologic toxicity risks. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 24. Gentamicin and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity risks. Monitor renal function and adjust therapy. 25. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir and Tenofovir DF: This combination may increase tenofovir levels by reducing metabolism. Monitor for tenofovir-associated toxicities. 26. Ibuprofen (oral or IV) and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to reduced renal clearance. Monitor closely and consider alternatives. 27. Idelalisib and Doravirine: Idelalisib increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased plasma concentrations and adjust therapy as needed. 28. Imatinib and Doravirine: Imatinib increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for toxicities. 29. Indinavir and Lamivudine or Tenofovir DF: Both combinations increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 30. Isoniazid and Doravirine: Isoniazid increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased plasma concentrations and potential toxicities. 31. Interferon Alfa-2b and Lamivudine: Co-administration increases the risk of liver decompensation. Use caution and monitor liver function. 32. Istradefylline and Tenofovir DF or Doravirine: Istradefylline increases tenofovir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition and doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 33. Itraconazole and Doravirine: Itraconazole increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased plasma concentrations and potential toxicities. 34. Ketoprofen, Ketorolac, or Meloxicam and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to reduced renal clearance. Monitor closely and consider alternatives. 35. Lamivudine and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 36. Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir and Tenofovir DF: This combination increases tenofovir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor for tenofovir-associated toxicities. 37. Lenacapavir and Doravirine: Lenacapavir increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for toxicities. 38. Lopinavir and Doravirine: Lopinavir increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased plasma concentrations and potential toxicities. 39. Lorlatinib and Doravirine: Lorlatinib decreases doravirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 40. Mifepristone and Doravirine: Mifepristone increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for toxicities. 41. Mitomycin and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity risks. Monitor renal function closely. 42. Morphine and Tenofovir DF: Tenofovir increases morphine levels by reducing renal clearance, raising the risk of toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 43. Naproxen and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to reduced renal clearance. Monitor closely and consider alternatives. 44. Nelfinavir and Lamivudine or Tenofovir DF: Both combinations increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 45. Neomycin and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity risks. Monitor renal function closely. 46. Posaconazole and Doravirine: Posaconazole increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased plasma concentrations and potential toxicities. 47. Orlistat and Tenofovir DF or Lamivudine: Orlistat reduces the absorption of these drugs, potentially leading to virological failure. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently and discontinue orlistat if viral load increases. 48. Oxaliplatin and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity risks. Monitor renal function closely. 49. Pamidronate and Tenofovir DF: Pamidronate increases tenofovir levels by reducing renal clearance, raising the risk of nephrotoxicity. Use caution and monitor. 50. Peginterferon Alfa-2a or Alfa-2b and Lamivudine: Co-administration increases the risk of liver decompensation. Use caution and monitor liver function. 51. Pemetrexed and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity risks. Monitor renal function closely. 52. Probenecid and Tenofovir DF: Probenecid increases tenofovir levels by reducing renal clearance, raising the risk of toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 53. Ritonavir and Lamivudine or Tenofovir DF: Both combinations increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 54. Rucaparib and Doravirine: Rucaparib increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased plasma concentrations and adjust therapy as needed. 55. Safinamide and Tenofovir DF: Safinamide increases tenofovir levels by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Monitor for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects. 56. Stiripentol and Tenofovir DF: Stiripentol increases tenofovir levels by inhibiting BCRP transport. Monitor for adverse effects and consider dose reduction if necessary. 57. Streptomycin and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity risks. Monitor renal function closely. 58. Sulindac and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to reduced renal clearance. Monitor closely and consider alternatives. 59. Velpatasvir/Sofosbuvir and Tenofovir DF: This combination increases tenofovir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor for tenofovir-associated toxicities. 60. Sitagliptin and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to reduced renal clearance. Monitor closely. These interactions highlight the importance of careful monitoring, dose adjustments, and consideration of alternative therapies to minimize risks and optimize patient outcomes.
